==English==

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:fynden|tree=1}}
{{inh+|en|enm|fynden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|findan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*finþan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*finþaną}}, a secondary verb from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*pent-||to go, pass; path bridge}}.

See also {{cog|fy|fine}}, {{cog|nds|finden}}, {{cog|nl|vinden}}, {{cog|de|finden}}, {{cog|da|finde}}, {{cog|nb|finne}}, {{cog|nn|-}} and {{cog|sv|finna}}; also {{cog|en|path}}, {{cog|sga|étain||I find}}, {{m|sga|áitt||place}}, {{cog|la|pōns||bridge}}, {{cog|grc|πόντος||sea}}, {{cog|xcl|հուն||ford}}, {{cog|ae|𐬞𐬀𐬧𐬙𐬃}}, {{cog|sa|पथ|tr=pathá||path}}, {{cog|sla-pro|*pǫtь}}.

For the meaning development compare {{m+|sla-pro|*najьti}} > {{m+|ru|найти́}}, akin to {{m+|sla-pro|*jьti}} > {{m|ru|идти́}}; {{m+|ru|находи́ть}}, {{m|ru|нахо́дка}}, akin to {{m|ru|ход}}, {{m|ru|ходи́ть}}.

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L1317}}
[[File:Nymphs finding the Head of Orpheus.jpg|thumb|upright|"Nymphs Finding the Head of Orpheus", a painting by {{w|John William Waterhouse}}]]
{{en-verb|~s|~ing|found,fand<l:dialectal>|+,founden<l:archaic>}}

# To locate.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To encounter or discover by accident; to happen upon.
##: {{syn|en|come upon|encounter|happen across|run across|Thesaurus:discover}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''found''' this shell on the beach.}}
##: {{ux|en|She arrived home to '''find''' that the house had gone up in flames.}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Julius Caesar|II|i|passage=Searching the window for a flint, I '''found'''/This paper, thus sealed up.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1667|author=w:Abraham Cowley|title=The Request
|passage=Among the Woods and Forests thou art '''found'''.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=2|passage=I had occasion to make a somewhat long business trip to Chicago, and on my return, much to my surprise, I '''found''' Farrar awaiting me in the railway station.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[encounter]] or [[discover]] something being [[search]]ed for; to [[locate]].
##: {{syn|en|localize|pinpoint}}
##: {{ant|en|lose|miss}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''found''' my car keys. They were under the couch.}}
##: {{usex|en|I went looking for you in the bed we share, but tonight I '''found''' you not there.}}<!--Belongs with this sense if construed as "I did not find you there"-->
##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=10|passage=It was a joy to snatch some brief respite, and '''find''' himself in the rectory drawing–room. Listening here was as pleasant as talking; just to watch was pleasant.}}
##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-20|volume=408|issue=8845|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21581981-what-pollution-some-opportunity-others-welcome-plastisphere Welcome to the plastisphere]|passage=
Plastics are energy-rich substances, which is why many of them burn so readily. Any organism that could unlock and use that energy would do well in the Anthropocene. Terrestrial bacteria and fungi which can manage this trick are already familiar to experts in the field. Dr Mincer and Dr Amaral-Zettler '''found''' evidence of them on their marine plastic, too.}}
## {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To locate on behalf of another.
##: {{ux|en|I '''found''' you a new place to live}}
# {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To [[discover]] by study or experiment directed to an object or end.
#: {{ux|en|Water is '''found''' to be a compound substance.}}
#: {{ux|en|The researchers '''found''' the two variables to be strongly correlated.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:CBC News|title=Problem gambler crackdown coming to B.C. casinos|date=August 18 2011
|text=The B.C. Lottery Corporation commissioned two independent studies that '''found''' its voluntary self-exclusion program isn't always catching gamblers who've requested help in staying away.
|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/problem-gambler-crackdown-coming-to-b-c-casinos-1.1126994|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260906064051/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/problem-gambler-crackdown-coming-to-b-c-casinos-1.1126994|archivedate=6 September 2026}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To gain, as the object of desire or effort.
#: {{ux|en|to '''find''' leisure; to '''find''' means}}
#* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|format=full|Revelation|9|6|folio=cccxxix|verso=1|passage=And in thoſe dayes ſhall men ſeke deeth / and ſhall nott '''fynde''' hyt / ſhall deſyre to deye / and deeth ſhall flye frõ them.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To attain to; to arrive at; to acquire.
#: {{syn|en|gain|get|obtain|Thesaurus:acquire}}
#: {{ant|en|lose|Thesaurus:lose}}
#: {{ux|en|Looks like he '''found''' a new vehicle for himself!}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[meet with]]; to [[receive]].
#: {{uxi|en|The proposal '''found''' little support within the government.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[point out]].
#: {{ux|en|He kept '''finding''' faults with my work.}}
# {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To decide that, to conclude that, to form the [[opinion]] that, to [[consider]].
#: {{syn|en|consider|hold|look upon|Thesaurus:deem}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''find''' your argument unsatisfactory.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''found''' it strange {sleeping - to sleep} in your house last night.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|II|i|passage=I '''find''' you passing gentle.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1647|author=w:Abraham Cowley|title=The Request
|passage=The torrid zone is now '''found''' habitable.}}
#* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=1|passage=“ the awfully hearty sort of Christmas cards that people do send to other people that they don't know at all well. You know. The kind that have mottoes And then, when you see [the senders], you probably '''find''' that they are the most melancholy old folk with malignant diseases.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1987|month=October|volume=172|number=4|title=Results of the Smell Survey|author=Avery N. Gilbert and Charles J. Wysocki|page=516
|text=Of those respondents who detected an odor, most '''found''' it musky/urine, many others floral.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To arrive at, as a conclusion; to determine as true; to establish.
#: {{ux|en|to '''find''' a verdict; to '''find''' a true bill (of indictment) against an accused person}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 5|I|ii|passage=to '''find''' his title with some shows of truth}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To supply; to furnish.
#: {{ux|en|to '''find''' food for workmen}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To provide for.
#: {{ux|en|He '''finds''' his nephew in money.}}
#* {{RQ:Kingsley At Last|volume=I|page=135|passage=They stand idle in the market-place, not because they have not been hired, but because they do not want to be hired; being able to live like the Lazzaroni of Naples, on "Midshipman's half-pay—nothing a day, and '''find''' yourself."}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1892|author=W. E. Swanton|title=Notes on New Zealand
|passage=the pay is good, the musterer receiving ten shillings a day, and all '''found''', all the time he is engaged on the "run," even should he be compelled to remain idle on account of rain or mist.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|law}} To [[determine]] or [[judge]].
#: {{syn|en|decide|make a decision|Thesaurus:decide}}
#: {{ux|en|The jury '''finds''' for the defendant.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|ball sports}} To successfully pass to or shoot the ball into.
#: {{ux|en|Peters '''finds''' Jinkins, who is running down the left wing.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=January 25, 2011|author=Paul Fletcher|work=BBC|title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/9371217.stm Arsenal 3-0 Ipswich (agg. 3-1)]|passage=
{{w|Robin van Persie|Van Persie}} scored a hat-trick against {{w|Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan}} on Saturday and should have '''found''' the net again after Bendtner '''found''' him at the far post but the Dutchman's header rebounded to safety off the crossbar.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|hunting}} To discover game.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1945|author=w:Nancy Mitford|title=The Pursuit of Love|page=57|publisher=Penguin|year_published=2010
|passage=They '''found''' at once, and there was a short sharp run, during which Linda and Tony, both in a somewhat showing-off mood, rode side by side over the stone walls.}}

===Noun===
{{wikidata lexeme|L16739}}
{{en-noun}}

# Anything that is found (usually valuable), as objects on an archeological site or a person with talent.
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=2001
|author=Chün-fang Yü
|chapter=Feminine Forms of Kuan-yin in Late Imperial China
|title=Kuan-yin: The Chinese Transformation of Avalokiteśvara
|url=https://archive.org/details/kuanyinchinesetr0000ychn/
|location=New York
|publisher=w:Columbia University Press
|ISBN=0-231-12028-1
|LCCN=00-024015
|OCLC=971596367
|page=409
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/kuanyinchinesetr0000ychn/page/409/
|text=One of the most exciting '''finds''' made by Chinese archaeologists within the last twenty years are the sites located in Inner Mongolia and Liaoning Province, particularly the Neolithic Hung-shan culture (c. <small>3500-2500 B.C.E.</small>).}}
# The act of finding.
#: {{rfex|en}}
